newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen Expressway seen strong on debut.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen Expressway seen strong on debut.

text.p: Expressway developer and operator Shenzhen Expressway Co Ltd's H-shares are poised for a strong trading debut on Wednesday, repeating the story of Shum Yip Investment Ltd, analysts said.

"Shum Yip and Shenzhen Expressway are both closely tied with their Shenzhen parents, they are similar to each other in many ways, they are both tapping the strong growth in Shenzhen," said Patrick Chia, research manager at China Everbright Research.
Brokers said the recent strong debut of new listings also boosted sentiment surrounding initial public offerings.
Shares of the Shenzhen-municipal government backed Shum Yip soared 144.6 percent to close their market debut at HK$4.525 on Friday.
Leather garments manufacturer and distributor Peking Apparel International Group Ltd also ended Friday debut 86 percent up from its offer price of HK$1.00.

Analysts said expectation of an increase in traffic flow between Hong Kong and Shenzhen following the Hong Kong's handing over to Chinese ruling in July, also boosted the prospects of Shenzhen Expressway.
Shenzhen Expressway operates and manages two class one highways and has a 55 percent stake in two co-operative expressway joint ventures in Shenzhen.

It issued 650 million H-shares at price ranging HK$2.00 to HK$2.20 each in flotation, of which 10 percent of the issue offered to the public in Hong Kong and the remaining 90 percent for professional and institutional investors.
Market sources said the Hong Kong public offering portion of the new issue was expected to be about 40 times subscribed. The company is due to announce the subscription results on Tuesday.
Sources said they expected the share to be priced at the upper end of the range.
H-shares are shares of Chinese enterprises which listed in Hong Kong.

"As Shenzhen Expressway shares are offered at about 18 percent discount to its NAV (net asset value) per share of about HK$2.58, it has room on the upside compared with another toll road concern Anhui Expressway which trades at about five to 10 percent discount to NAV," said Frankie Szeto, analyst at Tai Fook Securities.
Anhui Expressway Co Ltd was listed in November. Its shares closed at HK$2.275 on Monday compared their issue price of HK$1.77.

"I think the shares will be fairly valued if the stock trades at about five percent discount to NAV or trade at par," Szeto said. Some analysts said the stock would be fairly valued it traded at a premium to NAV.
Shenzhen Expressway said proceeds would be used to fund the construction of Jihe Expressway (west), to repay indebtness and for working capital.
